answers.explanation: HA with sync failover = Multi-AZ (RDS) or Aurora storage-layer redundancy. Standby is not for reads. night-15-rds-aurora.md Multi-AZ table.
Lambda connection storms → RDS Proxy pools to Aurora/RDS. night-15-rds-aurora.md RDS Proxy section.
Spiky PostgreSQL + auto scale = Aurora Serverless v2. v1 scale-to-zero is legacy; v2 keeps min ACU.
Read scaling = async read replicas. Multi-AZ standby is not a read endpoint on standard RDS.
Sub-second cross-Region RPO + secondary reads = Aurora Global Database.
JOINs + FKs + ACID = relational (Aurora/RDS). DynamoDB for simple key access (wiki counters).
Aurora storage auto-scales to 128 TiB — no manual GB provisioning. Classic exam trap.
DR failover to replica = manual promote; breaks replication chain. Async lag may apply.
Multi-AZ sync for HA; read replicas async for scale. Flashcard #1.
RDS automated backup retention 1–35 days with PITR. night-15-rds-aurora.md backups table.
Serverless v2 does not scale to zero ACUs. Stop/start RDS or teardown dev for idle savings.
DB SG inbound from app SG on DB port — Night 8 quiz callback; night-16 lab preview.
RDS Proxy is the serverless→relational pooling answer. Multi-AZ does not add connection slots for reads on standby.
Backtrack = Aurora MySQL-compatible only. PostgreSQL uses PITR from automated backups.
Right tool per access pattern: DynamoDB counters vs Aurora relational stats. GSA architecture diagram in night-15-rds-aurora.md.
